{{Current events|year=2018|month=01|day=15|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Iraqi Civil War (2014–present)]], [[January 2018 Baghdad bombings]]
**A double suicide bombing kills at least 35 people and injures over 90 in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]]. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-42686677 (BBC)]
*[[India–Pakistan military confrontation (2016–present)]]
**Four [[Pakistani army|Pakistani soldiers]] are killed in shelling by the [[Indian Army]] across the disputed [[Kashmir]] frontier. [https://in.reuters.com/article/pakistan-india/four-pakistani-soldiers-killed-in-indian-fire-across-tense-kashmir-frontier-idINKBN1F4129 (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Turkey]] threatens to "strangle" the [[United States]]-backed [[Syrian Border Security Force]] "before it's even born", while [[Syria]] vows to crush it and expel American military personnel from the country. [[Russia]] called the plans "a plot to dismember Syria". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria/erdogan-we-will-strangle-u-s-backed-force-in-syria-before-its-even-born-idUSKBN1F41HJ (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[Caracas helicopter incident]]
**Two [[Law enforcement in Venezuela|police]] officers and several gunmen are killed near [[Caracas]] in an operation to capture [[Óscar Pérez (policeman)|Óscar Pérez]], the rogue pilot responsible for the Caracas helicopter incident on June 27, 2017, according to the [[Government of Venezuela|Venezuelan government]]. Five people have also been arrested. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-42695537 (BBC)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Weinstein effect]], [[Me Too (hashtag)|#MeToo]]
**[[Americans|American]] actress [[Eliza Dushku]] says she was [[child sexual abuse|sexually assaulted]] by a stuntman when she was 12 years old. [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2018/jan/15/eliza-dushku-accuses-true-lies-crew-member-of-sexually-assaulting-her-aged-12 (''The Guardian'')]

;Business and economy
*After talks between the company, its lenders, and the [[United Kingdom]]'s government fail to reach a deal, [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[facilities management]] and construction services company [[Carillion]] fails and is [[liquidation|liquidated]], threatening thousands of jobs. Carillion is currently involved in projects such as the [[high-speed rail in the United Kingdom]], including the [[High Speed 2]] rail line. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-42687032 (BBC)]
*[[List of largest rough diamonds]]
**A 910 [[Carat|ct]] "[[Diamond color#Grading the normal color range|D colour]] [[Diamond type#Type IIa|Type II A]]" [[Diamond (gemstone)|diamond]] is dug up in the [[Letseng diamond mine]], [[Lesotho]]. [http://www.miningmx.com/top-story/31327-gem-share-flies-910-carat-whopper-recovered-letseng/ (''MiningMX'')] 

;Disasters and accidents
*The [[mezzanine]] overlooking the main lobby of the [[Indonesia Stock Exchange]] in [[Jakarta]], [[Indonesia]], collapses, injuring at least 70 people. The [[Indonesian National Police]] ruled out terrorism as the cause. [http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/world/indonesia-floor-collapses-at-jakarta-stock-exchange/news-story/3446f9650f112f4621bdab69f6a15b50 (''The Australian'')], [https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/904727/Indonesia-stock-exchange-floor-collapse-evacuation-casualties (''Daily Express'')]
*The [[Mayon]] volcano begins to erupt in the [[Philippines]].  [http://www.cnn.com/2018/01/15/asia/mayon-volcano-alert-level-increased/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Chirajara bridge collapse]]
**A partially completed bridge in Cundinamarca, [[Colombia]], collapses, killing at least 10 workers. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-accident/collapse-of-colombian-bridge-kills-nine-workers-injures-five-idUSKBN1F42JS (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[2017–18 North Korea crisis]], [[Korean War]]
**A meeting of senior officials from countries that backed South Korea in the Korean War begins today in Vancouver which will look at ways to better implement sanctions to push North Korea to abandon its nuclear weapons. China and Russia, which backed the North in the war but have since agreed to U.N. sanctions on Pyongyang, will not be attending the meeting. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles-diplomacy/vancouver-meeting-focuses-on-sanctions-as-koreas-explore-detente-idUSKBN1F42MQ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Palestine relations]]
**[[Nabil Shaath]], the foreign affairs adviser of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, says that the [[Palestinian Central Council]] freezes its recognition of the state of [[Israel]] until Israel recognizes [[State of Palestine|Palestine]] as a state. Palestine will freeze the Oslo accords. [http://www.gulf-times.com/story/573704/US-Jerusalem-recognition-would-end-Trump-peace-pus (Gulf News)]

;Law and crime
*Aftermath of the [[2013 Lahad Datu standoff]]
**[[Malaysia]] upholds death sentences for nine Filipino [[Tausūg people|Tausūgs]] over 2013 incursion in [[Sabah]] by a faction of claimant to the [[Sultanate of Sulu]] throne.  [https://in.reuters.com/article/malaysia-security-invasion/malaysia-upholds-death-sentences-for-nine-filipinos-over-2013-incursion-idINKBN1F414M?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A knife fight between students breaks out in a school in [[Perm]], [[Russia]]. Twelve injured are reported, with three of them in serious condition. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-42688457 (BBC)]
*Two people are arrested in [[Perris, California]], after 13 people aged between 2 and 29 years old are found being held captive at their house, including some "shackled to their beds with chains and padlocks". They are all believed to be siblings. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-42698562 (BBC)] 
*[[Chinese espionage in the United States#2010-2012 compromise of CIA network|Chinese espionage in the United States]]
**Jerry Chun Shing Lee, a former U.S. [[Central Intelligence Agency]] officer, is arrested at New York's [[John F. Kennedy International Airport|Kennedy International Airport]] and held without bail by the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York|Brooklyn federal court]].  He faces charges that, after he left his job, he kept notebooks filled with classified information about undercover agents and assets which he allegedly used to help China identify [[informant]]s and [[CIA activities in China#Dismantling of CIA Operations|dismantle a U.S. spying network]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-cia-officer/ex-cia-officer-arrested-for-retaining-classified-information-idUSKBN1F52SE (Reuters)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/01/16/us/politics/cia-china-mole-arrest-jerry-chun-shing-lee.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/public-safety/ex-cia-officer-charged-with-taking-notebooks-full-of-classified-information/2018/01/16/1f629634-fb06-11e7-a46b-a3614530bd87_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Egypt]]
**The nephew of assassinated [[Egyptian president]] [[Anwar Sadat|Mohamed Anwar al-Sadat]] announces that he will not run in [[Egyptian presidential election, 2018|March’s presidential election]], blaming an environment of fear surrounding the vote. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/jan/15/sadat-nephew-and-sisi-critic-drops-egyptian-presidential-bid (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Politics of Romania]]
**[[Romania]]n [[Prime Minister of Romania|Prime Minister]] [[Mihai Tudose]] resigns after losing the support of the [[Social Democratic Party (Romania)|Social Democratic Party]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-romania-government-pm/romanias-pm-resigns-after-losing-partys-backing-idUKKBN1F42IZ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Rohingya persecution in Myanmar (2016–present)|Rohingya persecution in Myanmar]]
**Win Myat Aye, Myanmar's minister of social welfare, relief and resettlement, announced that his country would begin [[Repatriation|repatriating]] [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] [[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh|refugees]] in [[Bangladesh]] beginning on January 23, 2018. Burmese officials also promised that a newly built camp for repatriated refugees would also be finished by that date. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/myanmar-says-1st-camp-for-rohingya-will-be-ready-next-week/2018/01/15/7415cea2-fa58-11e7-9b5d-bbf0da31214d_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/myanmar-camps-rohingya-ready-week-52350604 (ABC News)]
*[[Partition and secession in California]]
**A group of Californians criticize their state government and declare their desire to form a new U.S. state called [[New California]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/articles/2018-01-16/activists-seek-to-create-51st-state-new-california (''U.S. News & World Report'')]
*[[Politics of the United States]]
**Nine out of the twelve members of the U.S. [[National Park Service]]'s advisory board resign out of protest over their treatment by Interior Secretary [[Ryan Zinke]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/health-science/nearly-all-members-of-national-park-service-advisory-panel-resign-in-frustration/2018/01/16/b322ef5e-fae3-11e7-ad8c-ecbb62019393_story.html (''The Washington Post'')], [https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2018/01/17/578525840/majority-of-national-park-service-board-resigns-citing-administration-indifference (NPR)]
